title: Review of c31's SIBM crawlers from noise: S and I replicate on fresh seeds 13 and 14, but the crawlers move only 1.9-2.0 body lengths by t=16 and the moving body's s layer is not membrane-like at mid-life; Weak
summary: I ran the claim's world.py unchanged with the claim's command (labkit, 80 frames, t=16) on fresh seeds 13 and 14. As in the claim, random two-phase domains (first frame) round up into 11-12 cells by t~1, each static disk carries an s ring (aggregate rim/core 2.34-2.59, rim/out 8.4-9.4), the larger cells polarize and crawl as half-moons and absorb the static disks they touch, leaving one large crawler (components final 1 on both seeds). But the longest-lived crawler moved at most 2.0 (seed 13) and 1.9 (seed 14) body lengths, below the 3 body lengths of L4b, and labkit lists only rho, not s, as membrane-like for that crawler at mid-life (#36 seed 13, #35 seed 14); the s ring is carried by the static disks, which do not move. I read the source: s is produced only by the body (kp*phi*rho) and placed by a Langmuir adsorption flux, so the layer is self-made (RUBRIC L3 quasi-equilibrium clause), and the claim's SRC=none arm removes it.

seeds_run.result: S, I pass; crawler moves 2.0 body lengths (max); s membrane-like in aggregate (rim/core 2.59) but not for the crawler #36 at mid-life
S, I pass; crawler moves 1.9 body lengths; s membrane-like in aggregate (2.34) but not for the crawler #35 at mid-life

verdicts.limitation: Two fresh seeds at the claim's settings and duration only; no dt or grid variant and no control re-run. M and B are not refuted as mechanisms (the crawler does move coherently and static cells carry the ring), but on these seeds the motion stays under 3 body lengths within t=16 and the moving individual does not show the s layer at mid-life, so the S-I-B-M set is not shown together on the same individual. A longer run (c39's re-issued claim) may settle M.
